result.rationale: The diff adds an awaited `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly in the SalesforceCalendarService constructor flow, executed on every service construction with no timeout. Previously jsforce's Connection handled refresh lazily; now a network failure (or non-OK status throwing HttpError) rejects the promise stored in `this.conn`, which can become an unhandled rejection if callers don't await a method that touches the connection. This is new behavior verifiable from the added lines in packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` the diff adds an unconditional `await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` refresh-token request before constructing the `jsforce.Connection`. This means the code path that builds the connection now performs a network call up front (and the `fetch` has no timeout/AbortSignal). However, the finding’s claim that this runs specifically “on every service construction” and that failures cause an “unhandled rejection when no method awaits it” is not fully verifiable from the diff alone because the constructor/usage of `this.conn` isn’t shown here.
